newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Bus strike leaves thousands stranded in Sri Lanka.
newsitem.headline: Bus strike leaves thousands stranded in Sri Lanka.

text.p: A bus strike crippled Sri Lanka's transport system on Wednesday, leaving thousands of commuters stranded.
Bus drivers, conductors and other workers in most of the island's 90 bus depots have been on strike since Monday, demanding a 40 percent pay hike, officials said.
A few private buses were running in Colombo where long queues formed at bus stops.

The depots, originally run by the government, were handed over in the early 1990s to employees who were given 10 percent of the shares and asked to run the depots as companies to generate larger profits.
But the government still pays the employees.

Transport Minister Mohammed Fowzie was quoted as saying by local newspapers on Wednesday that instead of generating profits, the bus depots had run up billions of rupees in losses largely due to corruption, mismanagement and inefficiency.
Fowzie said the depots' liabilities included seven billion rupees ($119 million) for buses provided by the government. They also owed several million rupees to suppliers for spare parts, he said.
The minister said he had offered union leaders a flat pay rise of 365 rupees ($6.2) per month and additional overtime pay.
But Transport Union leader James Kariyawasam said the strike would continue until the government agreed to a 40 percent pay hike.
Kariyawasam said more depots would stop services if an agreement could not be reached soon.
